record.original_question:
For arbitrary positive definite n×n matrices A and B and any positive
integer k, does the polynomial z ↦ Tr((A+zB)^k)
always have only nonnegative coefficients?

evidence.quote: Problem 39 (BMV Conjecture). Let n ∈ N and A, B be arbitrary positive  definite n × n matrices. Then for any k ∈ N the polynomial z 7→ Tr (A + zB)k has only non-negative coefficients.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $A, B$ be positive definite Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices. For every positive integer $k$, consider the polynomial
$$p_{A,B,k}(z) := \operatorname{Tr}\bigl((A+zB)^k\bigr) \in \mathbb{R}[z].$$
Prove or disprove: for all such $A$, $B$ and all $k \in \mathbb{N}$, every coefficient of $p_{A,B,k}(z)$ (as a polynomial in $z$) is nonnegative.

(Equivalently, this is the polynomial form of the Bessis–Moussa–Villani conjecture: the function $t \mapsto \operatorname{Tr}\exp(A - tB)$ on $[0,\infty)$ is the Laplace transform of a positive Borel measure on $[0,\infty)$ whenever $A$ is Hermitian and $B$ is positive semidefinite.)
artifact.status_search_result: The BMV conjecture (in its equivalent polynomial form about nonnegativity of coefficients of Tr((A+zB)^k)) was proved by Herbert Stahl in 2011 (preprint arXiv:1107.4875), with the final version published in Acta Mathematica 211 (2013), 255–290. A simplified proof was given by A. Eremenko (2015), and a further structural generalization implying Stahl's theorem was given by O. Heinävaara (2023).
